text: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth.
A day on Venus is longer than its year.
Venus rotates in the opposite direction to most other planets.
Neutron stars are so dense that a teaspoon of their material would weigh billions of tons.
Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined.
Saturn is light enough that it would float if you could find a bathtub big enough.
The footprints left on the Moon could last millions of years, since there is no wind to erase them.
There are more stars in the observable universe than grains of sand on all of Earth's beaches.
The Sun makes up about 99.8% of the mass of the entire solar system.
Olympus Mons on Mars is the tallest known volcano in the solar system, nearly three times the height of Everest.
A year on Mercury lasts just 88 Earth days.
The Milky Way and Andromeda galaxies are slowly drifting toward a collision billions of years from now.
Space is silent because there is no air to carry sound waves.
Light travels at about 299,792 kilometers per second.
Water expands when it freezes, which is why ice floats.
Honey never truly spoils; edible honey has been found in ancient Egyptian tombs.
Glass is not a slow-moving liquid; it is an amorphous solid.
Under the right conditions, hot water can freeze faster than cold water, an effect named after Erasto Mpemba.
A bolt of lightning is roughly five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
Helium was discovered in the Sun's light before it was ever found on Earth.
Diamond and graphite are both made entirely of carbon, just arranged differently.
Gallium is a metal that will melt in the warmth of your hand.
Sound travels roughly four times faster in water than in air.
Bananas are slightly radioactive because they contain potassium-40.
Oxygen is the most abundant element in the Earth's crust.
Absolute zero, about minus 273.15 degrees Celsius, is the coldest temperature possible.
The only letter that does not appear in the periodic table of elements is J.
Rubber bands last longer when kept refrigerated.
A single teaspoon of soil can contain more microorganisms than there are people on Earth.
Trees can share nutrients and warning signals through underground networks of fungi.
Bamboo is among the fastest-growing plants, sometimes growing nearly a meter in a single day.
Sunflowers can help draw certain toxins out of contaminated soil.
Some bristlecone pines have lived for more than 4,000 years.
Lightning strikes the Earth roughly 8 million times every day.
Mushrooms are more closely related to animals than to plants.
A single cloud can weigh more than a million pounds.
Antarctica is the largest desert on Earth.
Raindrops are not tear-shaped; falling drops flatten into a shape like a tiny bun.
On rare occasions, snow has fallen in the Sahara Desert.
Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood.
A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance.
Honeybees can learn to recognize individual human faces.
Wombats produce cube-shaped droppings.
Some snails can sleep for up to three years at a time.
Cows form close friendships and can become stressed when separated from a friend.
Sea otters sometimes hold hands while sleeping so they don't drift apart.
A shrimp's heart is located in its head.
Elephants are the only mammals that cannot jump.
Tardigrades can survive extreme cold, radiation, and even the vacuum of space.
Sloths can hold their breath longer than dolphins can.
Crows can remember human faces and seem to hold grudges.
A hummingbird's heart can beat more than 1,000 times per minute.
Starfish have no brains.
Butterflies taste with sensors on their feet.
A group of crows is called a murder.
Dolphins call to one another using signature whistles that work like names.
An ostrich's eye is larger than its brain.
Polar bears have black skin beneath their translucent fur.
Giraffes have the same number of neck vertebrae as humans: seven.
A jellyfish is roughly 95% water.
Koalas have fingerprints so similar to ours they could be confused at a crime scene.
A cat can make over 100 different sounds, while a dog makes about ten.
More than 80% of the ocean has never been explored or mapped in detail.
The longest mountain range on Earth runs underwater along the mid-ocean ridge.
The Pacific is the largest and deepest of Earth's oceans.
The Mariana Trench reaches nearly 11 kilometers below the ocean surface.
We have more detailed maps of Mars than of much of our own ocean floor.
Your body is home to more bacterial cells than human cells.
The human nose can distinguish over a trillion different scents.
Bone is stronger than steel by weight.
Your brain uses about 20% of your body's total energy.
Stomach acid is strong enough to dissolve certain metals.
You are about a centimeter taller in the morning than at night.
The human heart beats roughly 100,000 times a day.
Adults have 206 bones, but babies are born with around 300.
Your taste buds are replaced roughly every two weeks.
The cornea receives no blood supply; it takes oxygen directly from the air.
The small intestine is about six meters long.
A sneeze can leave your body at over 100 kilometers per hour.
Your body creates around 25 million new cells every second.
The Great Pyramid of Giza remained the tallest human-made structure for nearly 4,000 years.
Oxford University was teaching students before the Aztec Empire existed.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
The shortest war in recorded history lasted about 38 minutes, between Britain and Zanzibar in 1896.
Napoleon was once swarmed by a horde of rabbits during a hunting trip.
The Eiffel Tower can grow more than 15 centimeters taller in summer as the metal expands in the heat.
Vikings never actually wore horned helmets; that image came from later artists.
The earliest oranges from Southeast Asia were green, not orange.
In the 1830s, ketchup was sold as a medicine.
The Great Wall of China cannot be seen from space with the naked eye.
Wristwatches became popular partly because soldiers needed them in World War I.
The Statue of Liberty was a gift from France to the United States in 1886.
The Hundred Years' War actually lasted 116 years.
The first recorded Olympic Games were held in 776 BC in ancient Greece.
Tea bags were invented by accident, first used as sample packaging.
Ancient Egyptians sometimes slept on curved headrests of stone or wood instead of soft pillows.
The most common letter in written English is E.
A pangram is a sentence that uses every letter of the alphabet at least once.
The dot over a lowercase i or j is called a tittle.
The word quarantine comes from an Italian phrase meaning forty days.
The shortest complete sentence in English is: I am.
Bookkeeper is one of the few English words with three consecutive double letters.
The word robot comes from a Czech word meaning forced labor.
Mandarin Chinese has more native speakers than any other language.
The symbol & is called an ampersand.
No common English word forms a perfect rhyme with orange, silver, or purple.
The word nerd first appeared in a Dr. Seuss book.
Uncopyrightable is one of the longest English words with no repeated letters.
Carrots were originally purple and white long before orange ones became common.
Peanuts are not true nuts; they are legumes, like peas and beans.
Apples float in water because about a quarter of their volume is air.
The Aztecs valued cacao beans so highly that they used them as money.
Cucumbers are about 96% water.
Almonds are members of the same family as peaches.
A banana is botanically a berry, but a strawberry is not.
Ripe cranberries bounce like little rubber balls.
Saffron is one of the most expensive spices in the world by weight.
Pineapples can take around two years to fully grow.
Russia spans eleven time zones.
Africa is the only continent that lies in all four hemispheres.
Canada has more lakes than the rest of the world combined.
The Dead Sea is so salty that swimmers float without any effort.
Australia is wider from coast to coast than the diameter of the Moon.
Vatican City is the smallest country in the world.
Parts of the Atacama Desert in Chile are among the driest places on Earth.
Istanbul is a major city that sits on two continents at once.
Mount Everest grows a few millimeters taller each year as tectonic plates push upward.
The Nile is generally regarded as the longest river in the world.
A googol is the number 1 followed by 100 zeros.
In a group of just 23 people, there is about a 50% chance two share a birthday.
Any whole number multiplied by nine has digits that add up to a multiple of nine.
The digits of pi never settle into a repeating pattern.
The Fibonacci sequence shows up throughout nature, from sunflower seeds to spiral shells.
A jiffy is a real unit of time, often defined as about one hundredth of a second.
Multiplying 111,111,111 by itself gives 12,345,678,987,654,321.
Zero cannot be written as a standard Roman numeral.
The first computer mouse was carved out of wood.
The first webcam was set up to watch a coffee pot at a university in Cambridge.
QWERTY keyboards were designed in the 1800s for mechanical typewriters.
The first message sent over the ARPANET was meant to be LOGIN, but the system crashed after LO.
Email existed years before the World Wide Web was invented.
The Firefox logo actually depicts a red panda, not a fox.
Wi-Fi is a marketing name and does not officially stand for anything.
The @ symbol was used by merchants long before it became part of email addresses.
Early hard drives the size of refrigerators could store only a few megabytes.
A group of pandas is called an embarrassment.
Wearing headphones for even an hour can greatly increase the bacteria in your ear.
The Hawaiian alphabet has only 13 letters.
A flock of ravens is sometimes called an unkindness.
The dot of an i, the tail of a comma, and other tiny marks are what make handwriting feel personal.
